Chronic Care Management (CCM)

The Care Coordination That Happens Between Appointments

Chronic care management is a Medicare program that reimburses non-face-to-face care coordination for patients with two or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months. It covers the work that happens between visits: medication management, care plan updates, coordinating with specialists, and checking in on a patient who's managing diabetes, hypertension, COPD or another ongoing condition alone at home.

That coordination work has always happened informally in most practices, a nurse calling a patient, a staff member following up on a referral, but it rarely gets billed because tracking the required 20 minutes of monthly clinical time per patient, documenting it correctly, and building a comprehensive care plan is its own administrative burden on top of an already full day.

PMEX identifies eligible patients, builds and maintains comprehensive care plans, tracks monthly time against the CPT requirement, and documents everything to CMS standards, so the coordination work your practice already does becomes a billable, sustainable program instead of unpaid overhead.

CCM Billing Codes

Four Codes for Different Levels of Complexity

CPT 99490

Standard CCM

First 20 minutes of clinical staff time coordinating care for the month.

CPT 99439

Additional 20 Minutes

Each additional 20-minute block beyond the first, billed as needed.

CPT 99487

Complex CCM

First 60 minutes for patients needing complex, moderate-to-high complexity decision making.

CPT 99489

Complex, Additional

Each additional 30-minute block for complex CCM beyond the first 60 minutes.

Performance Reporting

Enrollment, time logged and billing status reported so the program's impact stays visible.

Chronic Care Management: Frequently Asked Questions

Medicare patients with two or more chronic conditions expected to last at least 12 months, or until the patient's death, and that place the patient at significant risk of decline, are eligible for CCM.

Yes. Patients must give verbal or written consent to enroll in CCM, including acknowledgment of any applicable cost-sharing, and that consent is documented as part of enrollment.

Non-face-to-face care coordination time, including phone calls with the patient, medication reconciliation, care plan updates, and coordination with other providers involved in the patient's care.

Yes, both programs can run for the same patient, as long as the time counted toward each program's requirement is tracked separately and not double-billed.
